territorial_scope.description: Applies to the direct procurement of electricity via the electricity supply network in Peninsular Malaysia.

evidence.quote: via Electricity Supply Network in Peninsular Malaysia

summary.short: Malaysian Energy Commission guidelines, issued under section 50C of the Electricity Supply Act 1990, setting rules for the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS). They let Green Consumers buy electricity directly from renewable energy developers over the Peninsular Malaysia network, with applications opening from 30 September 2024.
summary.long: The Guidelines, issued by the Energy Commission under section 50C of the Electricity Supply Act 1990, set the procedure and conditions for the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS) in Peninsular Malaysia. Under the CRESS, a Renewable Energy Developer (RED) owns and operates a Green Energy Plant (GEP) that supplies a Green Consumer through Open Access to the grid, with the Electricity Utility Company (EUC) acting as supplier of last resort. Participants must register under the New Enhanced Dispatch Arrangement, sign several contracts, and meet requirements including at least 51% local ownership, a GEP of at least 30MW with Direct Connection, and, where firm output is not provided, an energy storage system of at least 50% of registered capacity for four hours or a higher System Access Charge. The System Access Charge is fixed for three-year regulatory periods with a maximum variation of 15%, and excess energy may be sold to the system at 8 sen/kWh. The Commission reserves the right to revoke participant registration for construction delays or non-compliance. The text states no penalty amounts. Applications start from 30 September 2024.

notes: Guidelines issued by the Energy Commission under section 50C of the Electricity Supply Act 1990. Version history on the cover is partly illegible (GP/ST/No.40/2024 (Pindaan 2025), revisions dated 1 March 2025 and 29 December 2025, third version undated); the signature date is 26 December 2025. Clause 2 sets commencement at registration, and no registration date is stated in the text. Clause 13.1 says applications start from 30 September 2024, which is earlier than the 26 December 2025 signature date. Clause 3.1 'Regulations' definition is split and partly garbled in the source. Appendices 1 and 2 use 'TNB' and 'ESA' where the body text uses EUC and CRESA. Clause 14.1 records that participants waive legal actions against the Commission, Single Buyer, GSO and EUC for matters connected with the guidelines. Relations only cover instruments named in the text; no registry IDs were verified.

thresholds.value_text: at least fifty one percent (51%) local ownership
thresholds.consequence: RED must meet the local ownership minimum; this shall be part of the licence condition.
thresholds.conditions: RED must operate in Peninsular Malaysia.

evidence.quote: The RED shall be operating in Peninsular Malaysia with at least fifty one percent (51%) local ownership which shall be part of the licence condition.

thresholds.variable_text: energy storage capacity as share of GEP registered capacity
thresholds.value_text: not less than fifty percent (50%) of the GEP registered capacity or the tested capacity prior to commercial operations whichever lower
thresholds.measurement: lower of GEP registered capacity or tested capacity prior to commercial operations
thresholds.consequence: Where the GEP cannot fulfil the Firm Output requirement, RED must develop an energy storage system with Direct Connection; the alternative is a higher System Access Charge.
thresholds.conditions: Storage must discharge for four (4) consecutive hours and be dispatchable by GSO as per system requirement; applies where GEP is unable to fulfil the Firm Output requirement.

evidence.quote: The energy storage capacity (MW) shall not be less than fifty percent (50%) of the GEP registered capacity

thresholds.variable_text: maximum variation rate of SAC revision
thresholds.value_text: a maximum variation rate of 15% from the prevailing charge
thresholds.measurement: variation from the prevailing System Access Charge
thresholds.consequence: Any revision to the System Access Charge may not vary by more than 15% from the prevailing charge and takes effect only at the start of a new Regulatory Period.
thresholds.conditions: Applies to revisions of the SAC under the Incentive Based Regulation Regulatory Period.

thresholds.consequence: GEP becomes subject to decommissioning, and must be removed by RED within twelve (12) consecutive months or within the period specified in the decommissioning plan.
thresholds.conditions: Also applies if the GEP has ceased operation.
